clinicalPearls: Caused by loss of the LCHAD activity of the mitochondrial trifunctional protein, most often from the common c.1528G>C (p.Glu474Gln) variant in HADHA; the trifunctional protein catalyses the final three steps of each long-chain beta-oxidation cycle.

Distinctive long-term complications set it apart from most other fatty-acid-oxidation disorders: a progressive pigmentary chorioretinopathy causing visual loss and a length-dependent peripheral neuropathy.
Acute presentation overlaps with other long-chain defects, with hypoketotic hypoglycaemia, cardiomyopathy, hepatopathy, sudden collapse and exercise-induced rhabdomyolysis.
Newborn screening shows accumulation of long-chain hydroxyacylcarnitines, notably 3-hydroxypalmitoylcarnitine (C16-OH) and 3-hydroxyoleylcarnitine (C18:1-OH).
Carrying an affected foetus predisposes the mother to acute fatty liver of pregnancy and to HELLP syndrome, an obstetric clue that should prompt testing of the infant.
Isolated LCHAD deficiency, in which only the LCHAD activity of the alpha subunit is impaired, is generally milder than complete trifunctional protein deficiency affecting all three activities.

Dietary management mirrors other long-chain disorders (fasting avoidance, long-chain-fat restriction, medium-chain triglyceride) with additional docosahexaenoic acid supplementation aimed at slowing the retinopathy.
reference.pathophysiology: The mitochondrial trifunctional protein is an inner-membrane complex assembled from alpha subunits (HADHA) carrying long-chain enoyl-CoA hydratase and long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCHAD) activities and beta subunits (HADHB) carrying long-chain 3-ketoacyl-CoA thiolase activity. When the LCHAD activity is deficient, oxidation of long-chain 3-hydroxyacyl-CoA esters halts, so long-chain 3-hydroxy fatty acids and their acylcarnitines accumulate while hepatic ketogenesis fails during fasting, giving hypoketotic hypoglycaemia and energy deficit in heart and muscle. The accumulating hydroxylated intermediates are thought to be directly cytotoxic and are implicated in the retinal pigmentary degeneration and peripheral nerve injury that are unique to this disorder, and in the maternal hepatotoxicity seen when a heterozygous mother gestates an affected foetus whose hydroxy-fatty-acid metabolites enter the maternal circulation.
additionalDifferentials: Inherited retinal dystrophies such as retinitis pigmentosa syndromes
Peroxisomal disorders with retinopathy and neuropathy
additionalInvestigations: Plasma acylcarnitine profile showing raised long-chain hydroxyacylcarnitines
Urine organic acids with 3-hydroxydicarboxylic aciduria during metabolic crisis
Molecular testing of HADHA and HADHB
Trifunctional protein enzyme or fatty-acid flux assay in cultured fibroblasts
Ophthalmological assessment with fundoscopy, electroretinography and optical coherence tomography
Nerve conduction studies for the peripheral neuropathy
redFlags: Hypoketotic hypoglycaemia with cardiorespiratory collapse in an infant
New or worsening cardiomyopathy or arrhythmia
Rhabdomyolysis with myoglobinuria and threatened acute kidney injury
Maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy or HELLP syndrome in a current or previous pregnancy
Rapidly declining vision suggesting progression of the chorioretinopathy
reference.prognosis: Even with treatment the retinopathy and neuropathy tend to be progressive, and early cardiac decompensation can be fatal. Newborn screening and strict dietary management improve survival and reduce the frequency of metabolic crises.
pitfalls: Neglecting retinal and neurological surveillance because acute metabolic control looks satisfactory
Failing to test the infant after maternal acute fatty liver of pregnancy or HELLP syndrome
Conflating isolated LCHAD deficiency with complete trifunctional protein deficiency, which carries different severity and counselling
Administering long-chain lipids during an acute crisis
references: Fatty acid oxidation disorder management consensus guidelines
management: Prevent catabolism by avoiding fasting with frequent carbohydrate-rich feeds and, in infants, overnight feeds or uncooked cornstarch to maintain glucose supply
Restrict dietary long-chain fat and substitute medium-chain triglyceride oil, which bypasses the blocked long-chain beta-oxidation, while ensuring essential fatty acid provision
Supplement docosahexaenoic acid to slow the progressive pigmentary chorioretinopathy
Institute an emergency regimen during intercurrent illness with intravenous glucose to abort hypoketotic hypoglycaemia and rhabdomyolysis

Monitor for disorder-specific complications with serial echocardiography for cardiomyopathy, ophthalmological review with electroretinography for retinopathy, nerve conduction studies for neuropathy and creatine kinase for rhabdomyolysis
Coordinate care through a metabolic physician, specialist dietitian, cardiologist and ophthalmologist multidisciplinary team
Provide genetic counselling for this autosomal recessive disorder with cascade family testing, and highlight the maternal risk of acute fatty liver of pregnancy and HELLP syndrome
Escalate promptly for acute metabolic decompensation, cardiac failure or exertional rhabdomyolysis
